subject: general
question: Kulhads are disposable cups made of clay. A little thought shows that making these kulhads on a large scale would result in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**losing the fertile top-soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kulhads are made from clay, which is sourced from the top layer of the soil.
 
• The top-soil is the most fertile part of the soil, containing essential nutrients for plant growth.
 
• Excessive removal of this top layer for making kulhads can lead to soil degradation and reduced agricultural productivity.
 
• Loss of fertile top-soil adversely affects crop yields, impacting food security and farmers' livelihoods.
 
• Soil erosion and desertification can be accelerated by the removal of the top-soil layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Top-soil**

 
 
• The uppermost layer of soil, typically 5-20 cm deep, rich in organic material and microorganisms.
 
• It is crucial for plant growth, as it holds water and nutrients.
 
• Top-soil conservation is essential for sustainable agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Soil Degradation**
 
 
• The decline in soil quality caused by its improper use or poor management.
 
• It can result from erosion, loss of soil structure, and nutrient depletion.
 
• Soil degradation leads to reduced agricultural productivity and ecological imbalance.
 
 
 
• **Soil Conservation Methods**
 
 
• Practices such as crop rotation, cover cropping, and contour plowing help in preventing soil erosion.
 
• Maintaining vegetation cover and applying organic matter improve soil structure and fertility.
 
• Soil conservation is vital for long-term agricultural sustainability and environmental health.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture**
 
 
• Loss of fertile top-soil reduces the land's agricultural potential.
 
• Farmers face lower crop yields and increased costs for fertilizers and soil amendments.
 
• Sustainable soil management practices are necessary to ensure food security and rural livelihoods.
